bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Mental Health Nurse Salary

When exploring a **mental health nurse salary**, it is important to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage and the specific award rates that apply to nurses. The Nurses Award 2020 (MA000034) sets minimum pay and conditions for most nurses in Australia, including those working in mental health settings. This article explains how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, the role of casual loading, and how superannuation and tax affect take-home pay.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, bringing the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour. However, most nurses are covered by the Nurses Award, which provides higher minimum rates. For example, a registered nurse at Pay Point 1 earns $30.00 per hour, well above the national minimum.

### Mental Health Nurse Salary Under the Nurses Award

Under the Nurses Award, full-time employees work 38 hours per week (or an average of 38 hours). The minimum weekly rate for a nurse at Pay Point 1 is $1,139.90, which equates to $30.00 per hour. This is the base rate before any allowances, penalty rates, or overtime. For a mental health nurse, the annual salary (gross) is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For Pay Point 1: $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year.

If you are a casual mental health nurse, the casual loading of 25% is added to the base rate, giving $37.50 per hour. The annual gross for a casual working 38 hours per week would be $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. However, casuals do not receive paid leave, so the higher hourly rate compensates for that.

For part-time nurses, the rates are applied pro-rata based on the 38-hour full-time week. The award also includes pay points for experience: Pay Point 2 ($30.39/hr), Pay Point 3 ($30.80/hr), Pay Point 4 ($31.24/hr), and Pay Point 5 ($31.56/hr). These rates are updated annually through the Fair Work Commission's [pay guides](/blog) and the Annual Wage Review.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual loading is an additional 25% on the minimum hourly rate, as per clause 11.1 of the Nurses Award. This loading is applied to the base rate before any penalty rates or overtime. For a mental health nurse, the casual rate is clearly higher, but it is important to remember that casual employees do not accrue annual leave or sick leave.

Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time nurse earning $1,139.90 per week, the employer contributes an extra $136.79 per week to super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This super is not deducted from the nurse's pay; it is an additional benefit. For casuals, super is also paid on the casual hourly rate (including loading) because the loading is part of ordinary earnings.

## Converting Hourly to Annual

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a mental health nurse at Pay Point 1 working 38 hours per week, the annual gross is $59,280. For a casual at $37.50 per hour, it is $74,100.

You can also calculate fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly rate by 2. For a full-time nurse, the fortnightly gross is $2,279.80. This is useful for budgeting and understanding pay cycles.

## Take-Home Pay Considerations

After gross pay, tax and the Medicare levy are deducted. For the 2026–27 financial year, the tax-free threshold is $18,200, with marginal rates of 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a full-time mental health nurse earning $59,280, the estimated tax (using the 2026–27 rates) would be approximately $7,717, plus Medicare of $1,186, leaving a take-home pay of about $50,377 per year. This is an estimate and does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

For more detailed calculations, you can use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) reference tables or the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide. Remember that the figures here are based on the Nurses Award and the National Minimum Wage; actual pay may vary depending on experience, location, and employer agreements.

## Conclusion

A mental health nurse salary under the Nurses Award is significantly higher than the National Minimum Wage. Full-time nurses at Pay Point 1 earn $30.00 per hour, with higher rates for experienced nurses. Casual nurses receive a 25% loading, and superannuation is paid on top. When converting hourly to annual, always use 38 hours per week unless your contract specifies otherwise. For accurate pay calculations, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) and the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database.
